This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
Order Was Made Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice S.R.Krishna Kumar

 Oral Order
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice S.R.Krishna Kumar)

In this petition, the petitioners seek the
following reliefs:
"a) Issue Writ of Certiorari/order/direction, quashing the order/endorsement issued
by the respondent No.2 - Deputy Commissioner, Vijaypur, in File
No.REVENUE/RB/VIVA-
19/2017-18, Dated 21.10.2023 vide Annexure-A and consequently all the respondent authorities
may be directed to pay the compensation of the petitioners land bearing Sy.No.97/1A measuring 5
acres situated at Honnutagi village, Tq. & Dist. Vijaypur having utilized for the purpose of graveyard
along with all monetary benefits, damages, interest as per Land Acquisition Act forthwith.

b) Issue writ of mandamus/direction, directing the respondent authorities, to put the petitioners
into the possession and enjoyment of their land bearing Sy.No.97/1A measuring 5 acres situated at
Honnutagi village, Tq. & Dist. Vijaypur, by getting stopped the burial/cremation of dead bodies, in
case, the Government is not interested in paying the compensation to the petitioners land within a reasonable time.

c) Issue any other appropriate order, as deemed fit and proper by this Hon'ble Court, including the cost of the present Writ Petition payable to the petitioner to meet the ends of justice and equity."
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned HCGP for respondent Nos.1, 2 and 4 to 6 and perused the material on record.

3. In addition to reiterating the various contentions urged in the petition and referring to the material on record, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the land bearing Sy.No.97/1A measuring 5 acres belonging to the petitioners was taken over by the respondents, who formed Siddawwa And Ors vs State Of Karnataka And Ors on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120508451/
3 graveyard in the said land without taking recourse to acquisition proceedings nor acquiring the same by following due process of law.

sentences.text: Further, when the petitioners made request to the respondent to give compensation or allot alternative land, the respondents took a decision to allot alternative land in Sy.No.84 to an extent of 5 acres in view of the aforesaid land in Sy.No.97/1A measuring 5 acres taken over from the petitioners and utilised for the purpose of graveyard without acquisition proceedings or following due process of law.

Since repeated representations of the petitioners to consider allotment of alternative land was not complied with by the respondents, petitioners approached this Court in W.P.No.201477/2023, which was disposed of by this Court vide NC:
2024:KHC-K:9493 final order dated 27.06.2023, pursuant to which respondent No.2 proceeded to pass the impugned order directing allotment of alternative land in Sy.No.276 measuring 5 acres instead of Sy.No.84 of Honnutagi Village.
Aggrieved by the impugned communication at Annexure-A dated 21.10.2023, the petitioners are before this Court by way of the present petition.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that despite a categorical/definite/specific finding recorded by this Court that the respondents has identified alternative land at Sy.No.84 measuring 5 acres issuing specific directions to the respondents to allot alternative land in an extent of 5 acres,
failing which the respondents shall allot some other land in some other area fixing the same price,
the respondents have rejected the request for allotment of 5 acres in Sy.No.84 by assigning untenable reasons and as such, the impugned communication deserves to be set aside and necessary directions be issued to the respondents to allot land in Sy.No.84 to an extent of 5 acres in favour of the petitioners.
5.

In this context, learned counsel for the petitioners invited my attention not only to the impugned communication, in NC: 2024:KHC-K:9493 order to point out that the reasons assigned by respondent No.2 that the land in Sy.No.84 was being used for different purpose is false and in reality 5 acres of land in Sy.No.84 is actually available for allotment for grant in favour of the petitioners.
It is also submitted that other reasons assigned in the impugned communication as regards value of Sy.No.84 is not only incorrect, but contrary to the order passed by this Court.

6. Per contra, learned HCGP would support the impugned communication and submit that since the value of the land in Sy.No.84 was much higher than the land of the petitioners coupled with the fact that no land is actually available in Sy.No.84, in which houses are already been built, the impugned communication does not warrant interference by this Court and the writ Petition is liable to be dismissed.
7.

Before adverting to rival submissions, it would be profitable to extract the earlier order passed by this Court in W.P.No.201477/2023 dated 27.06.2023, wherein the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court held as under:

sentences.text:
The petitioners are before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
"1) Issue writ of mandamus to respondent No.2/Deputy Commissioner Vijayapura to consider requisitions of the petitioner dated 22.11.2022 (Annexure-L), and dated 20.12.2022 and 16.06.2022 (Annexures- M and N) and to act in accordance with the decision taken on 13.12.2022 by Dist. Price Determination Committee, Vijayapura (Annexure-K) and consequently to send necessary report to respondent No.1/
Principal Secretary, Revenue Department, for final approval, to grant 5 acres alternative agricultural land as compensation to the petitioners in Govt. Land situated in land Sy.No.84/1 of Honnutagi Village, in lieu of petitioners 05 acres of land in Sy. No. 97/1A, which is now being unauthorizedly used as grave yard by public of Honnutagi Village, due to absence of public grave yard.
2) To issue writ of mandamus to respondent No.1/ Prl.
Secretary, Revenue Department, to give final approval for grant of alternative agricultural land to the petitioners within 04 weeks from the date of receipt of report from respondent No.2 / Deputy Commissioner Vijayapura, in the interest of justice."
NC: 2024:KHC-K:9493 3.
The petitioners herein are the wife and daughters of Honnappa Malakappa Pattanshetty, the owner in possession of land in Sy.No.97/1A measuring 5 acres of Honnutagi village.
The said land without any permission, acquisition or authorization was put to use as a graveyard and continued to be so done.

In that background, petitioner's husband and father had made a representation to the respondent-authorities to take appropriate steps to acquire the land and make payment of compensation and when no action was taken, the petitioners have approached this Court in W.P.No.207308/2015 when this Court vide order dated 06.02.2015 directed the Tahsildar to pass appropriate orders on the representation made by the petitioners and on the resolution passed by the Gram Panchayat dated 07.07.2006 within a period of three months.

However, no action was taken even in relation to the said order passed, subsequently there are various other proceedings which took place finally, the Price Determination Committee headed by the Deputy Commissioner,
Vijayapura, made an offer for a sum of Rs.16,00,000/- to the petitioners for purchase of the said land which was refused by the petitioners.
Subsequently, the land in Sy.No.84 of the very same village was identified from and out of which an extent of 5 acres was to be allotted to the petitioners.

However, no action being taken in relation thereto, the petitioners are before this Court seeking for the following reliefs.
4.
The land of the petitioners being used for graveyard is not in dispute and several correspondence and communications between the respondents in relation thereto.

Though initially an offer of Rs.16.00 lakhs was NC: 2024:KHC-K:9493 made for purchase of the land of the petitioner, the petitioner not being agreeable, the land in the Sy.No.84 was identified for the purpose of allotment to the petitioner, if that be so, it is for the respondents to have acted on the same and transfer an extent of 5 acres to the petitioner at the earliest, the same not having been done, I am of the Siddawwa And Ors vs State Of Karnataka And Ors on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120508451/

As such, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The writ petition is allowed in part.

ii. A mandamus is issued directing the respondent No.1 to identify and demarcate and allot a similar extent of land as that belonging to the petitioners which has been used for graveyard in a similarly situate area fetching the same price, if such land is not already available in the said Sy.No.84.
iii.
The above direction is to be complied within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order."

8. As is clear from the aforesaid order passed by this Court in the said petition filed by the petitioners herein, positive directions have been issued to the respondents to allot 5 acres of land in sy.No.84 in favour of the petitioners

; the said order further directs that it is only in the event that no land is available in Sy.No.84 that the respondents should allot alternative land in a similarly situated area fixing same price only if such a land is not - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:9493 available in Sy.No.84.

As stated supra, in view of the rival contentions/submissions urged by both sides as regards availability/non-availability of land in sy.No.84, it would be just and appropriate to set aside the impugned communication directing the respondents to conduct joint survey in the presence of the petitioners, identify and obtain a report as regards availability of 5 acres of land in Sy.No.84 for the purpose of allotment in favour of the petitioners.

It is also necessary to issue further directions to the effect that in the event such land is not available in sy.No.84, the respondents would allot alternative land in the same vicinity/area or initiate proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation Act and pay compensation in favour of the petitioners for taking over and utilizing Sy.No.97/1A without acquisition proceedings and without following due process of law.

9. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Writ Petition is allowed.
(ii) The impugned communication at Annexure-A dated 21.10.2023 is hereby quashed.

(iii) The following directions are issued to the respondents:

6 a) The respondents are directed to conduct joint survey in the presence of the petitioners for the purpose of identifying availability of land in Sy.No.84 to an extent of 5 acres to be allotted/granted in favour of the petitioners.

sentences.text: b) The said survey shall be conducted within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

c) In the event said land is available as per the joint inspection report, the respondents shall allot the said available land in favour of the petitioners within a period of three months from the date of obtaining the joint survey/inspection report.

d) In the event, no such land is available in Sy.No.84 is concerned, respondents shall allot alternative land in the same area/vicinity as Sy.No.84 in favour of the petitioners within a period of three months from the date of obtaining the report.

In the event no such alternative land other than Sy.No.84 is also not available for allotment, the respondent shall take necessary steps to initiate proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation Act, and pay compensation to the peititoner within a period of six months from the date of obtaining the report.
